decisions.new:
# Research status

## Rational-root heights restrict the quadratic indices

The [structural sequel](research/ai/2026-10-23-quadratic-kernel-indices/dichotomy.md)
shows that a minimum recurrence vector either has degree at least
`ceil((a-1)D/2)` or comes from a rational root of height h and degree
`(a+1)h`. It proves this through explicit polynomial Hankel kernel bases
and the arbitrary-field matrix-polynomial index-sum theorem. An irreducible
homogeneous quadratic forces the higher range; a sufficiently low rational
root height determines both indices exactly. As a concrete consequence,
the complete nonzero fifteen-by-fifteen biform-block rank spectrum at
a=b=3 is `{9,12,14,15}` over every field. Rank thirteen is impossible,
and explicit universal witnesses attain all four remaining values.
Claim `AI-QUADRATIC-INDEX-DICHOTOMY-002` is written and unreviewed.
This does not classify all slices of the full cyclic tensor or supply
an exponent improvement.

source_claim.title: Rational-root height dichotomy and the complete three-by-three biform rank spectrum
source_claim.origin: Codex research directed by repository owner
source_claim.statement: Under AI-QUADRATIC-KERNEL-INDICES-001, let D be the primitive coefficient degree, L=ceil((a-1)D/2), U=floor(aD/2), and h the smallest K(x)-rational root height of the homogeneous z-quadratic, or infinity. Then min(L,(a+1)h)<=mu1<=min(U,(a+1)h). A minimum recurrence vector has Hankel rank two and degree at least L, or rank one and is a primitive coherent root vector of degree (a+1)h. Thus homogeneous irreducibility forces mu1 in [L,U], and (a+1)h<=L fixes both indices. For a=b=3, the nonzero biform-block rank spectrum is exactly {9,12,14,15} over every field, with universal witnesses; rank thirteen is impossible.
dependencies: De Teran-Dopico-Mackey, MIMS EPrint2013.47, August22 2013, Theorem6.5 over arbitrary fields
Explicit polynomial left and right Hankel kernel bases, primitive Gauss lemma, and coherent rank-one classification
source_claim.limitations: These are necessary index restrictions, not a classification of all splitting types. The complete rank spectrum concerns the fifteen-by-fifteen biform block, not every slice of the full cyclic tensor. No source-space cap, three-leg target, degeneration, independent review, formalization, historical priority or exponent improvement.

primary_reference.title: Spectral equivalence of matrix polynomials and the index sum theorem
primary_reference.authors: Fernando De Teran, Froilan M. Dopico, D. Steven Mackey
primary_reference.verification: Primary PDF opened and theorem checked. It applies to arbitrary rectangular matrix polynomials over arbitrary fields and equates structural/minimal-index totals with grade times rational-function rank.

checked_arguments: A minimum recurrence vector is primitive, and its a-by-three Hankel matrix has normal rank one or two.

For Hankel rank two, the primitive coefficient triple generates the entire polynomial right kernel with index D. Its a-2 shifted rows generate the polynomial left kernel by primitive Gauss lemma and have independent leading coefficients, all indices D; a=2 has no left indices.
The external index-sum theorem then gives (a-1)D<=2 delta. The grade is exactly delta because all recurrence-vector coordinates occur in the Hankel matrix.

For Hankel rank one, primitive geometric sequences are coherent powers of a coprime rational-root pair; degree is (a+1) times its height, including both endpoints. Minimality makes the height minimal among rational roots.
Combining the root-vector upper bound with the two rank branches gives min(L,(a+1)h)<=mu1<=min(U,(a+1)h); equality at (a+1)h=L is covered.

D=0 remains a separate zero-index case: a constant irreducible quadratic need not have a ground-field root. Homogeneous irreducibility, endpoint roots, and inseparable characteristic-two cases are treated explicitly.

For a=b=3, D=0/1/2 and the dichotomy exclude rank13. The degree-two vector for the rank14 witness satisfies all recurrence equations and no degree<=1 vector exists; the rank15 witness has seven displayed blocks with determinant product -1, hence remains invertible over every field.
limitations_retained: Necessary index restrictions do not classify all attainable splitting types.
The {9,12,14,15} spectrum is for the fifteen-by-fifteen biform block, not every full cyclic-tensor slice.
No source-space cap, compatible three-leg map, degeneration, independent review, formalization, historical priority, or exponent improvement.
